name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals, a saddle or seat, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph. Defined by Code of Alabama §32-1-1.1(16) and regulated by §32-5A-267, both from HB 99 (Act 2021-134).
restrictions: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may be propelled by the motor alone, to 20 mph
The motor must disengage when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
Carries a permanent label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers of any age must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
As on any bicycle, riders and passengers under 16 must wear a helmet on a public road, path or park
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, shoulders, bike lanes and bicycle or multi-use paths
After notice and a public hearing, a county or city may ban Class 1 and 2 from a bicycle or multi-use path for safety or legal reasons, and may ban Class 3 outright
Those local path rules don't cover natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle: no driver's license, registration, title, plate or insurance
Excluded from Alabama's motor-driven cycle and off-road vehicle laws
